title: Finding Your Way Around the Terminal
description: Seven commands for the terminal footing this step assumes: print the current folder, list files, go home, make a course folder, and move between folders.

steps.description: The terminal always has a current folder, and every relative path is measured from it. `pwd` prints the folder you are in. `ls` lists what is here, and the comment notes `ls -la` also shows hidden files. `cd ~` goes to your home folder, and `mkdir -p ~/cs374` makes a folder for this course.
`cd ~/cs374` goes into the course folder. `cd ..` goes up one level, and `cd tests` goes into a folder named tests, relative to where you are.

steps.question: The page says paths that begin with `/` are absolute. What are paths without a leading slash measured from?
